persona: Upset about the break-in, answers quickly. Says the laptop was bought in March. Has one receipt, the Police reference and a photo of the window.
initial_message: Hello, my flat was broke in on Thursday 24th when I am at work. The thief come in through bathroom window and take my laptop and my headphone. I already report to the Police.

facts.incident.description: While I was at work someone forced the bathroom window of my flat and took my laptop from the desk and my headphones from the lounge.
facts.theft.entry_context: The bathroom window latch was forced open
facts.contents.receipt_availability: Receipt for the laptop available now; no receipt for the headphones
facts.policyholder.name: Wei Chenmoor
facts.evidence.photos: A photo of the forced bathroom window. Available now.
facts.evidence.police: The Police reference confirmation. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_date: I bought it in March. I do not know why the receipt says 26 September.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo from inside a small apartment bathroom, looking at an aluminium-framed frosted window that has been forced open from outside. The window latch is visibly bent and twisted out of shape and hangs loose from the frame. Deep fresh pry marks and gouges in the aluminium frame right next to the latch, bare silver metal showing, small flakes of white paint and metal shavings on the windowsill. Daylight. The damaged latch is in the centre of the frame, close up. No people, no text, no logos.
materials.purpose: Shows how the burglar got in
Proof of purchase for the laptop

data.summary: Burglary at 3/15 Tidewater Test Street, Sydenham, Christchurch. Entry through bathroom window. Laptop and headphones taken.

triage.rationale: The laptop receipt (serial KA14-TST-0419) prints a purchase date of 26 September 2026, two days after the theft on 24 September 2026. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and it is a material that contradicts the statement whether or not the Agent asks when the laptop was bought; the claimant's "March" only confirms it. Allowed but not required: the headphones have no receipt (evidence_outstanding); the claimant answers "I do not know why" to a clarification question (question_unanswered); the Agent may record that the laptop may not be fully covered because the schedule states no portable-electronics sublimit (coverage_unclear; a lookup uncertainty marker or such an Agent record is the only basis for it). None of them changes the class.

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Receipt purchase date 26 September 2026 is after the last possible incident day, 24 September 2026

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 January 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2023-01-20, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
